name: Caerdroea

attributes.attribute: Welsh word for the city of Troy
known to the Welsh as Caerdroea
older name for Troy carried in the Welsh title

text: Caerdroea is the Welsh word for the city of Troy. Ilium is the older title for that same town. The Welsh tongue held its own form for the famous place. This city lay far from Britain in ancient days. Yet the Welsh people gave the town a name of their own. The Trojan names fade since the royal line of Britain came from Troy. Brutus led that fabled descent. His tales crown the city with a royal weight inside Celtic story.

okr.objective: Present Caerdroea as the Welsh word for Troy and Ilium in the Trojan tradition.
key_results: give Caerdroea as the Welsh word for Troy
note that Caerdroea may stand for Ilium
link the royal Trojan tradition to the British kings
